items.description: Analyze repository structure and existing infrastructure
items.acceptance_criteria: Written document in results/phase1/repo_analysis.md listing all modules (.archivara/concept_evolve.py, .archivara/semantic_scholar.py, .opencode/ tools and agents), their purposes, data flow between them, and how they will be used in this research project. Must identify the concept_evolve tree output path (results/concept_evolve/tree/) and confirm empty figures/ and results/ directories are ready.

items.description: Conduct comprehensive web search for recent papers on univalent Bloch constant and related bounds (2009–2026)
items.acceptance_criteria: Web search covering at least these queries: 'univalent Bloch constant lower bound', 'schlicht Bloch constant', 'Bloch-Landau constant improvements', 'Skinner 2009 citations', 'Carroll Ortega-Cerda conformal welding Bloch', 'Bhowmik Sen meromorphic Bloch 2023 2024', 'Kudryavtseva Solodov Landau univalence domain', 'computational Bloch constant', 'Polya-Chebotarev extremal problem numerical'. Results documented in results/phase1/web_search_log.md with at least 20 distinct paper titles, authors, years, and relevance summaries.

items.description: Build citation graph using Semantic Scholar around Skinner 2009 and Carroll–Ortega-Cerdà 2009
items.acceptance_criteria: Use semantic_scholar tool to run 'graph' and 'citations' commands for both Skinner 2009 (DOI: 10.1080/17476930903197199) and Carroll–Ortega-Cerdà 2009 (J. Math. Pures Appl. 92(4), 396–406). Produce results/phase1/citation_graph.json containing at least 30 papers in the combined citation network. Identify the 5 most-cited successor papers and flag any post-2020 papers that cite both.

items.description: Deep-read and summarize key techniques from Skinner 2009 (current best lower bound B_u > 0.5708858)
items.acceptance_criteria: Written summary in results/phase1/skinner2009_analysis.md covering: (1) the iterative bootstrap method on the covering radius, (2) the implicit function C(|z|) and how it improves on the Koebe distortion bound B(|z|), (3) the role of the area theorem, (4) specific numerical steps that produce 0.5708858, (5) identified bottlenecks that limit further improvement. At least 1500 words.

items.description: Deep-read and summarize Carroll–Ortega-Cerdà 2009 upper bound technique (B_u ≤ 0.6564)
items.acceptance_criteria: Written summary in results/phase1/carroll_oc2009_analysis.md covering: (1) Goodman's slit-domain construction, (2) harmonic symmetry condition, (3) the Pólya-Chebotarev connection, (4) conformal welding, (5) the 3-fold symmetric extremal domain, (6) the explicit numerical value 0.6563937. Identify parameters that could be varied to potentially improve the upper bound. At least 1000 words.

items.description: Create and populate sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: File sources.bib in repo root contains valid BibTeX entries for at least 15 relevant papers including: Skinner 2009, Carroll–Ortega-Cerdà 2009, Bhowmik–Sen 2023, Yanagihara 1995, Bonk 1990, Chen–Gauthier 1996, Xiong 1998, Bonk–Minda–Yanagihara 1996, Ahlfors–Grunsky 1937, Ahlfors 1938, Goodman 1945, Rettinger 2008, Kudryavtseva–Solodov 2021, Jenkins 1992, Beller–Hummel 1985. Each entry must have author, title, journal/booktitle, year, and DOI (where available).

items.description: Delegate concept-tree exploration via subagent to map the mathematical landscape around B_u
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve tool with command 'evolve' on topic 'improving bounds on the univalent Bloch constant for schlicht functions'. Verify that results/concept_evolve/tree/ is populated with at least 10 concept folders, each containing concept.json, literature.json, and README.md. Produce results/phase1/concept_landscape.md summarizing the top-5 highest-adjacency concept nodes and their connections.

items.description: Implement Koebe distortion toolkit: reproduce classical bounds B(r) for univalent functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module results/phase2/koebe_distortion.py implementing: (1) Koebe distortion theorem bounds |f(z)| ≥ r/(1+r)^2, |f'(z)| ≥ (1-r)/(1+r)^3 for f ∈ S, (2) covering radius function B(r) = r/(1+r)^2 giving minimum |f(z)| on |z|=r, (3) the classical lower bound B_u ≥ sup_r B(r) = 1/4 (and the improved 1/2 argument). All functions tested with at least 3 unit tests in results/phase2/test_koebe.py that pass.

items.description: Reproduce Skinner's iterative bootstrap numerically
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module results/phase2/skinner_bootstrap.py implementing Skinner's implicit-function iteration: (1) define the implicit function C(|z|) from Skinner 2009 Theorem, (2) iterate to reproduce the bound B_u > 0.5708858, (3) output iteration-by-iteration convergence log showing how the bound improves at each step. Results match Skinner's published value to 7 decimal places. Convergence data saved to results/phase2/skinner_convergence.json.

items.description: Implement numerical conformal mapping toolkit for candidate extremal domains
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module results/phase2/conformal_map.py implementing: (1) Schwarz-Christoffel mapping for polygonal domains (using scipy or a custom implementation), (2) numerical Riemann mapping via Fornberg's method or zipper algorithm for slit domains, (3) function to compute the inradius (largest inscribed disk radius) of a given simply connected domain. Tested on the unit disk (inradius = 1), a square (known inradius), and a disk-minus-slit domain. At least 3 tests in results/phase2/test_conformal.py that pass.

items.description: Reproduce Carroll–Ortega-Cerdà upper bound numerically
items.acceptance_criteria: Python script results/phase2/carroll_upper_bound.py that: (1) constructs the Goodman-type slit domain with 3-fold symmetry used by Carroll–Ortega-Cerdà, (2) computes the conformal map from the unit disk to this domain, (3) estimates the largest inscribed disk in the image domain, (4) outputs B_u ≤ 0.657 or better (within 0.001 of the published 0.6564 value). Results saved to results/phase2/upper_bound_baseline.json.

items.description: Establish metrics framework and comparison table against prior work
items.acceptance_criteria: File results/phase2/metrics_baseline.md containing: (1) table of all known lower bounds for B_u with year, value, and method, (2) table of all known upper bounds with year, value, and method, (3) current gap analysis (0.6564 − 0.5708858 ≈ 0.0855), (4) comparison with related constants B, B_l, L and their gaps, (5) explicit target: state what improvement magnitude would be non-trivial (improving Skinner's lower bound by at least 10^{-4} or Carroll–OC's upper bound by at least 10^{-3}). References cite papers from sources.bib.

items.description: Explore concept tree paths for novel lower-bound strategies via subagent delegation
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve 'walk' command with depth ≥ 3 on the tree from item_007. Use the concept-tree-explorer subagent to identify the 3 most promising concept paths for improving the lower bound. Document findings in results/phase3/lower_bound_strategies.md with: (1) each path's concept chain, (2) the mathematical technique it suggests, (3) a feasibility assessment (high/medium/low), (4) expected improvement magnitude. At least one path must involve a technique not present in Skinner 2009 (e.g., variational methods, Loewner chains, or metric space arguments).

items.description: Develop extended Skinner bootstrap with higher-order distortion estimates
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module results/phase3/extended_bootstrap.py that: (1) incorporates second-order or Bieberbach-type coefficient constraints (|a_2| ≤ 2, |a_3| ≤ 3, etc.) into the bootstrap iteration, (2) uses the Grunsky inequalities or FitzGerald inequality to tighten the implicit function C(|z|), (3) runs the extended iteration and reports a lower bound. If the bound exceeds 0.5708858, document the improvement; if not, document why and what additional constraints would be needed. Results in results/phase3/extended_bootstrap_results.json.

items.description: Investigate variational/Loewner chain approach to characterize extremal domains for B_u
items.acceptance_criteria: Written analysis in results/phase3/variational_analysis.md covering: (1) formulation of B_u as a variational problem over S, (2) derivation of necessary conditions (Euler-Lagrange or Hamilton-Jacobi) for the extremal function, (3) connection to Loewner's differential equation (parametric representation of S), (4) what properties the extremal domain must satisfy (boundary regularity, symmetry, slit structure), (5) whether the extremal function is known to exist by compactness. At least 2000 words with mathematical derivations. Cites at least 5 papers from sources.bib.

items.description: Computational search over slit-domain configurations to improve the upper bound
items.acceptance_criteria: Python script results/phase3/slit_optimization.py that: (1) parameterizes families of slit domains (number of slits k ∈ {3,4,5,6}, slit radii, slit arc-lengths, rotational symmetry order), (2) for each configuration, computes the conformal map and the covering number, (3) uses numerical optimization (scipy.optimize or similar) to minimize the covering number over the parameter space, (4) reports the best upper bound found. Results saved to results/phase3/upper_bound_search.json. Must test at least 100 distinct configurations across k=3,4,5,6.

items.description: Explore Kudryavtseva-Solodov Landau-type approach for new lower bound pathway
items.acceptance_criteria: Written analysis in results/phase3/landau_approach.md covering: (1) summary of Kudryavtseva-Solodov 2021-2022 results on sharp invertibility domains for self-maps with boundary fixed points, (2) how their techniques relate to the chain B ≤ B_l ≤ L ≤ B_u, (3) a concrete proposal for how to leverage their sharp domains to improve either L or B_u bounds, (4) preliminary calculation or estimate showing potential improvement magnitude. References at least 3 papers. If a computable improvement to L > 0.5 + 10^{-335} follows, document the explicit new bound.

items.description: Mine literature graph for transferable ideas from meromorphic and harmonic Bloch theory
items.acceptance_criteria: Use the literature-graph-miner subagent to analyze Bhowmik-Sen 2023/2024 and related meromorphic/harmonic Bloch constant papers. Produce results/phase3/transferable_ideas.md identifying: (1) at least 3 techniques from the meromorphic setting that could transfer to the classical univalent setting, (2) for each technique, the precise adaptation needed, (3) expected impact on B_u bounds. Must cite at least 5 papers not already in sources.bib and add their BibTeX entries to sources.bib (total now ≥ 20 entries).

items.description: Run full lower-bound improvement experiments combining extended bootstrap and variational insights
items.acceptance_criteria: Python script results/phase4/lower_bound_experiments.py that: (1) implements the most promising approach from phase 3 items 013-015, (2) runs with multiple parameter settings (at least 10 configurations), (3) logs all intermediate bounds to results/phase4/lower_bound_log.json, (4) reports the best achieved lower bound with full numerical evidence. If B_u > 0.5709 is achieved, this constitutes a non-trivial improvement over Skinner's 0.5708858. Document the mathematical justification for each step's rigor.

items.description: Run full upper-bound improvement experiments with optimized slit domains
items.acceptance_criteria: Python script results/phase4/upper_bound_experiments.py that: (1) refines the best configuration from item_016, (2) uses higher-precision conformal mapping (at least 1000 mesh points), (3) verifies the upper bound by computing the covering number from multiple starting points in the image domain, (4) reports the best achieved upper bound with error estimates. If B_u < 0.6563 is achieved, this improves Carroll–OC's bound. Results saved to results/phase4/upper_bound_results.json.

items.description: Numerical search for candidate extremal functions/domains using Loewner chain discretization
items.acceptance_criteria: Python script results/phase4/extremal_search.py that: (1) discretizes the Loewner ODE with various driving functions (step functions, piecewise-linear, smooth), (2) for each generated function f ∈ S, computes B_f (the covering number), (3) searches for f minimizing B_f over at least 500 sampled driving functions, (4) reports the function with smallest B_f and its domain geometry. Results saved to results/phase4/extremal_candidates.json with the top-10 candidates' Taylor coefficients (a_2, a_3, ..., a_10) and their B_f values. Generate at least one figure in figures/extremal_domain_best.png showing the image domain of the best candidate.

items.description: Cross-validate all numerical results with independent high-precision computation
items.acceptance_criteria: Python script results/phase4/validation.py that: (1) re-computes the best lower bound from item_019 using mpmath with 50-digit precision, confirming the bound holds rigorously, (2) re-computes the best upper bound from item_020 with independent conformal mapping code, (3) verifies Skinner's baseline 0.5708858 to 10 decimal places, (4) checks internal consistency (lower bound < upper bound, all bounds between 0.5 and 1). Validation report saved to results/phase4/validation_report.md with pass/fail for each check.

items.description: Convergence and sensitivity analysis of all computational methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Results file results/phase4/sensitivity_analysis.md documenting: (1) convergence rate of the extended bootstrap iteration (how many iterations to stabilize), (2) sensitivity of the upper bound to slit parameters (partial derivatives w.r.t. each parameter), (3) mesh-size dependence of conformal mapping accuracy, (4) statistical summary of the extremal search landscape (distribution of B_f values). At least 2 figures saved in figures/ showing convergence curves and parameter sensitivity plots.

items.description: Synthesize all results into a comprehensive improvement claim with rigorous proof sketch
items.acceptance_criteria: Document results/phase5/main_result.md containing: (1) precise statement of the improved bound(s) achieved (e.g., 'B_u > X' or 'B_u < Y'), (2) complete proof sketch with all mathematical steps, (3) comparison table showing old vs. new bounds and the improvement magnitude, (4) discussion of which technique(s) contributed most to the improvement, (5) clear statement of what is rigorous vs. what depends on numerical computation. At least 3000 words.

items.description: Write updated constant card for C_57c with new bounds
items.acceptance_criteria: File results/phase5/constant_card_C57c.md in the format of TASK_orchestrator.md but updated with: (1) any new lower or upper bounds achieved, with full references, (2) updated Known lower bounds and Known upper bounds tables, (3) new references added to the References section, (4) contribution notes explaining the methodology. The card must be self-contained and citable.

items.description: Delegate final concept-tree synthesis to identify open problems and future directions
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept-tree-explorer subagent to re-traverse the concept tree from item_007, now annotated with experimental outcomes from phase 4. Produce results/phase5/future_directions.md listing: (1) at least 5 open problems ranked by tractability, (2) concept paths that were unexplored and why, (3) estimated difficulty and potential impact of each direction, (4) specific conjectures suggested by the computational evidence (e.g., conjectured extremal domain geometry, conjectured exact value of B_u if pattern emerges).

items.description: Compile final sources.bib and verify all citations
items.acceptance_criteria: Final sources.bib contains at least 25 valid BibTeX entries. Every paper cited in any results/ document has a corresponding entry. Run a check script that parses all .md files in results/ for citation keys and verifies each exists in sources.bib. Zero unresolved citations. Save check results to results/phase5/citation_check.json.

items.description: Generate summary figures and final research report
items.acceptance_criteria: At least 4 figures in figures/: (1) figures/bounds_timeline.png showing B_u lower and upper bounds over time (1925–2026) with our new result highlighted, (2) figures/gap_reduction.png showing the gap between bounds before and after this work, (3) figures/concept_tree_map.png visualizing the concept tree with explored/unexplored nodes, (4) figures/extremal_domain_best.png (from item_021). Final report results/phase5/final_report.md summarizing the entire research program in ≤ 5000 words, structured as: Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References.
